Sustainability.title: SUSTAINABILITY AND INTEGRATED MANAGEMENT SYSTEM POLICY
Sustainability.introduction: At SY Luxury Belek, we adopt an Integrated Management System (IMS) approach that plans, implements and continuously improves all our hotel operations in line with the principles of quality, environment, food safety, energy management, information security, legal compliance and social responsibility. This policy covers our guests, employees, suppliers, business partners and all stakeholders affected by hotel operations.

sections.title: QUALITY MANAGEMENT
items: We consider guest satisfaction a key performance indicator.
We continuously improve our service quality through a process-based management approach.
We ensure service continuity by supporting employee participation, training and competence.
We prioritize quality, continuity and reliability throughout our supply chain.

sections.title: ENVIRONMENTAL MANAGEMENT
items: We regard controlling our environmental impacts and protecting natural resources as a corporate responsibility.
We establish targets to reduce waste, increase recycling and encourage the use of environmentally friendly products.
We fully comply with environmental legislation and other relevant obligations.
We support local environmental projects and sustainable tourism.

sections.title: FOOD SAFETY MANAGEMENT
items: We consider food safety an essential part of guest health.
We prioritize hygiene, traceability and a risk-based approach in all food processes.
We fully comply with applicable food legislation and food safety standards.
We monitor our suppliers' compliance with food safety requirements.

sections.title: ENERGY MANAGEMENT
items: In line with our environmental responsibilities and legal obligations, we follow national and international standards and regulations, work to reduce energy consumption, monitor and measure our energy performance and pursue continuous improvement.
We commit to using energy resources efficiently and reducing our carbon footprint.
We support energy efficiency projects and raise employee awareness.
We assess energy-related risks and emergencies and plan appropriate preventive measures.

sections.title: SUSTAINABLE PURCHASING AND SUPPLY MANAGEMENT
items: We evaluate quality, food safety, environmental and energy criteria together in our purchasing processes.
We prioritize supporting local suppliers and local products.
We encourage our suppliers to adopt environmentally responsible, ethical, legally compliant and sustainable practices.
We emphasize traceability and continuity throughout our supply chain.

sections.title: SUPPORTING LOCAL EMPLOYMENT AND DEVELOPMENT
items: We aim to contribute to regional development by supporting local employment.
We prioritize products and services provided by local producers and service providers.
We contribute to protecting local cultural, social and economic values.

sections.title: HUMAN RIGHTS AND EQUALITY
items: We treat all employees, guests and stakeholders equally and fairly without discrimination based on religion, belief, language, race, color, gender, marital status, political opinion, age, disability or other personal characteristics.
We support a working and service environment in which people of different beliefs, thoughts and opinions can coexist with mutual respect and tolerance.

sections.title: CHILD PROTECTION AND SAFETY
items: We prioritize children's physical, emotional and psychological safety in all our activities.
We adopt a zero-tolerance approach to all forms of child abuse, neglect and mistreatment.
We fully comply with national and international legislation concerning children's rights.
We provide regular training to increase employee awareness of child protection and ensure that suspected incidents are reported to the relevant departments and competent authorities.

sections.title: OCCUPATIONAL HEALTH AND SAFETY
items: The health and safety of our guests, employees and business partners are as important as service quality. In keeping with our family-oriented hospitality approach, we assess occupational health and safety risks throughout our facilities and implement necessary preventive measures to protect all age groups.
We provide regular training to improve employee awareness of occupational health and safety.

sections.title: PERSONAL DATA PROTECTION AND INFORMATION SECURITY
items: We recognize the protection of our guests', employees' and stakeholders' personal data as a corporate responsibility.
We process personal data in compliance with Personal Data Protection Law No. 6698 (KVKK) and applicable regulations and securely destroy it when the applicable retention period expires.
We restrict access to personal data based on authorization and implement technical and administrative security measures.
We monitor information security risks and manage potential breaches through preventive and corrective actions.

sections.title: LEGAL COMPLIANCE, RISK AND CONTINUOUS IMPROVEMENT
items: We conduct all our activities in compliance with applicable national and international legislation.
We apply a systematic management approach by identifying risks and opportunities in advance.
We regularly review our Integrated Management System and continuously improve our performance.

Sustainability.conclusion: At SY Luxury Belek, we aim to implement this Integrated Sustainable Management System Policy together with all our employees and stakeholders, embracing a sustainable, safe, high-quality and environmentally responsible approach to hospitality.

ExploreRegion.title: EXPLORE THE REGION
ExploreRegion.description: To discover more of the natural and cultural treasures of our country and region, and to learn more about Turkish culture, we recommend visiting antalya.goturkiye.com, antalya.ktb.gov.tr and kulturportali.gov.tr.

kaleici.title: KALEİÇİ & OLD HARBOUR
kaleici.description: Located in the heart of Antalya, Kaleiçi offers a charming atmosphere with its narrow streets, traditional stone houses and historic buildings. Just below it, the Old Harbour is one of the city's most enjoyable places, with boats, cafés and beautiful sunset views.

manavgatWaterfall.title: MANAVGAT WATERFALL
manavgatWaterfall.description: Located 3 km west of Manavgat, the waterfall bears the same name as the district. Although it falls from a surprisingly low height, its roaring flow across a wide area creates a view well worth seeing. It can be reached by minibuses departing from Manavgat.

titreyengol.title: TİTREYENGÖL LAKE
titreyengol.description: The lake is very still, yet even the lightest breeze makes its surface tremble, which is how it got its name. According to legend, birds would gather around an old fisherman who lived by the lake whenever he fed them. One day, hunters shot ducks on the water. The fisherman confronted them and tried to stop the hunt, but they pushed him aside. The other ducks then rose together, creating a whirlwind with their wings and driving the hunters away. From that day on, the lake is said to have continued trembling.

side.title: SIDE
side.description: Located 75 km from Antalya and 7 km from Manavgat, Side is a peninsula approximately 400 metres wide and 1 kilometre long. The name Side means ‘pomegranate’ in an ancient Anatolian language. Inscriptions suggest that its history reaches back to the Hittites. According to some sources, one of Anatolia’s oldest settlements was founded before the 7th century BC and later came under the rule of many civilizations.

sideAncientCity.title: SIDE ANCIENT CITY
sideAncientCity.description: Located 75 km from Antalya and 7 km from Manavgat, Side lies on a peninsula approximately 400 metres wide and 1 kilometre long. Known in the lexicon of Hesychius as the City of Pomegranates, ancient Side brings history to life through its theatre, seaside ruins, Temple of Apollo, magnificent city gate, baths, agora and historic harbour.

aspendos.title: ASPENDOS THEATRE
aspendos.description: Built in the 2nd century AD, 44 km from Manavgat, the 17,000-seat Aspendos Theatre is one of the best-preserved amphitheatres still standing today. It is among the rare theatres whose stage has survived in excellent condition. The venue is now used for concerts, celebrations, festivals and traditional oil wrestling. The Agora, Basilica, Nymphaeum and 15-kilometre arched aqueducts are also worth seeing.

seleukeia.title: SELEUKEIA
seleukeia.description: The ruins of Seleukeia are reached after travelling 12 km northwest from Manavgat towards the Taurus Mountains. Founded by the Seleucids as a fortified acropolis city on a hill around 300 BC, its geography of steep slopes and deep valleys overlooks the entire plain and the sea.

kopruluCanyon.title: KÖPRÜLÜ CANYON
kopruluCanyon.description: Köprülü Canyon National Park is 60 km from Manavgat. It is one of Türkiye’s most popular rafting areas and its longest canyon. Rafting is an exciting river sport performed in inflatable boats on fast-flowing rivers. The Köprüçay River is one of Türkiye’s finest natural recreation areas, while Roman bridges, historic roads and many archaeological remains make the national park especially worth visiting.

kursunluWaterfall.title: KURŞUNLU WATERFALL
kursunluWaterfall.description: At Kurşunlu Waterfall, water falls from a height of 18 metres and seven small ponds are connected by smaller cascades. The waterfall lies within a two-kilometre canyon. Opened as a public park in 1986, the waterfall and picnic area cover 33 hectares and include viewing terraces, a children’s playground, restaurant, car park and walking paths.

saklikentCanyon.title: SAKLIKENT CANYON
saklikentCanyon.description: Located between Antalya and Fethiye, Saklıkent Canyon is 18 kilometres long. It is a rewarding destination for visitors planning a trip immersed in nature, where forests of Turkish red pine, cedar and black pine can also be seen.

alanyaCastle.title: ALANYA CASTLE
alanyaCastle.description: Alanya Castle is one of the symbols of Alanya, a district of Antalya. It stands on a peninsula rising approximately 250 metres above the sea, and its walls extend for a total of 6.5 kilometres. The castle was built during the Hellenistic period in the settlement once known as Kandeleri.

informationSections.title: RULES FOR VISITING NATURAL AND CULTURAL SITES
items: Do not touch or damage exhibits in museums. Do not take videos or photographs in prohibited areas, and follow all written or verbal instructions.
Do not damage ancient sites, enter protected areas or pollute their surroundings.
Do not picnic or light fires in natural recreation areas and forests. Never litter and always observe warning signs.
Do not behave inappropriately towards adults or children in these areas, and avoid disturbing other people.
Hunt only in accordance with the applicable laws and rules, and respect wildlife and the natural environment.
Do not buy or sell historical artefacts without the necessary permits and documents. Illegal trade is prohibited.
Remove your shoes before entering a mosque, observe the appropriate head-covering rules and do not bring food or drink inside.

To help protect nature, choose environmentally friendly cosmetics. Remember that chemicals entering water sources harm living organisms, while chemicals released into the atmosphere cause air pollution.

Check the opening days and hours of the museum you wish to visit. A Museum Pass lets you discover the country’s cultural and natural treasures while contributing to the protection of cultural heritage.

informationSections.title: BIODIVERSITY
paragraphs: Biodiversity is the variety of life forms found within an ecosystem and throughout the world. For people to survive, their environment must provide clean water and air, fertile soil, food and other necessities. Fungi, plants, animals and other living organisms that supply these needs together form biodiversity.

As biodiversity increases, the ecological services of an environment also increase, provided that the species involved interact in balance. Greater biodiversity makes nutrient cycles and energy flows more efficient; when biodiversity declines, ecosystem services decline as well.
Plant diversity cleans the air, prevents erosion, adds organic matter to the soil and reduces soil fatigue. By providing food and shelter for other organisms, plants give ecosystems continuity.

Humans have used animals since ancient times for food, transport, clothing and medical research. Some insects pollinate plants and sustain plant diversity; many help decompose organic matter and return it to the soil. Insects also provide food for birds, fish and reptiles.

The sustainability of ecosystems depends on the diversity and health of the species living within them. Preventing ecosystem degradation is essential to human survival. Biodiversity and ecosystems have their own intrinsic value and right to exist, beyond the benefits they provide to people. We must protect them not only for our needs, but because every living thing has a right to life.

informationSections.title: PROTECTED PLANT AND ANIMAL SPECIES IN OUR REGION
paragraphs: Mediterranean monk seals, sea turtles and Caretta caretta turtles are protected in our region. Plant species including vetch flowers, alkanet, irises, sea daffodils, broomrape, narcissus and crocuses are also among the protected species.

Do not purchase products made from protected plants or animals. Hunting outside the dates authorized by the Ministry of Agriculture and Forestry is prohibited. We strongly ask you not to attend circuses, zoos, dolphin shows or other activities that remove animals from their natural habitats.
